source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:11 ('the place-word written THREE times in the verse — a hint to the three pilgrimage festivals on which his children will ascend to that place'; Chullin 91b named)
claim_en: THE THREE PLACE-WORDS, PART 1: in the arrival verse (28:11) the place-word appears three times — twice with the in-prefix ('he ENCOUNTERED the place... he lay down IN THE PLACE'); this row counts the two prefixed tokens.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:11 (same note)
claim_en: THE THREE PLACE-WORDS, PART 2: the third token carries the the-prefix ('from the stones OF THE PLACE') — two prefixed plus one completes the Kitzur's three, the three pilgrimage ascents read in the letter's own repetition.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:11 ('כי בא השמש — the initials spell כבה, EXTINGUISHED: the sun's light was quenched not at its time')
claim_en: THE QUENCHED SUN IN THE INITIALS: כי בא השמש ('for the sun had come,' 28:11) — the three initials spell כבה ('it was EXTINGUISHED'): the sun set early for him, read straight off the first letters.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:12 ('מלאכי אלהים — two joined in the Masorah: here, and THEY MET HIM at Machanaim — the angels who escorted him in the land did not escort him outside it; those who ascended then met him on his return')
claim_en: THE ESCORT-ANGELS' TWO STATIONS: the construct pair מלאכי אלהים ('angels of God') stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — the ladder's ascending-and-descending angels at the exile's first night (28:12) and the camp that MEETS him at its end (32:2): the Kitzur's escort-exchange reading rides a two-token census.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:12 ('מוצב — three: here; the oak STATIONED at Shechem; I will lay siege against you with a POST — he was shown the entry to the land and the exile from it')
claim_en: THE ONE STATIONED-WORD OF THE TORAH: מצב ('the ladder STATIONED toward the ground,' 28:12) — the passive stationed-form's ONLY Torah token; the Masorah's other two stations are the oak at Shechem (Judg 9:6) and the siege-post (Isa 29:3) — the Kitzur reads entry and exile in the word's own later career (outside the instrument, named).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:13 ('והנה ה׳ — four in the Masorah: standing over him; standing on the plumb-wall; making windows in heaven; passing by — all chariot-work, and so here: THIS IS THE GATE OF HEAVEN')
claim_en: THE TORAH'S ONE 'AND BEHOLD — YHWH': והנה followed directly by the four-letter Name stands ONCE in the Torah — YHWH stationed over the ladder (28:13); the Masorah's other three (the plumb-wall of Amos, the windows of Kings, the passing of Horeb) are all Prophets-side, named — the Kitzur binds all four to the chariot-vision.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:12 ('השמימה — without pashta')
claim_en: HEAVENWARD AS RULED: השמימה ('its top reaching HEAVENWARD,' 28:12) carries no pashta (the forward-leaning accent) — the verse's rest (etnachta) sits on it instead, exactly per Minchat Shai; the full stored token is the proof.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:14 ('ובזרעך — no lengthening stroke on the vav')
claim_en: THE SEED-WORD'S BARE VAV: ובזרעך ('and IN YOUR SEED shall all families be blessed,' 28:14) — the vav carries no meteg (the small lengthening stroke), as Minchat Shai rules; the stroke the word does carry sits later, on the seed-syllable itself.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:15 ('אעזבך — the Michlol cites a Jerusalem manuscript pointing hataf qamatz on the root's first letter, and likewise I-will-serve-you of the wage; a GREAT ANOMALY in my eyes')
claim_en: THE PROMISE-VERB AGAINST THE ANOMALY: אעזבך ('I will not LEAVE YOU,' 28:15) — the root's first letter in hataf segol (the compound short e), NOT the Jerusalem manuscript's hataf qamatz that Minchat Shai calls a great anomaly: SNAPSHOT sides with him. (Its twin, I-will-serve-you of the wage-verse, waits in the next unit's span.)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:16 ('וייקץ — with two yods in all the precise books; the one-yod claim of Michlal Yofi is an error; the Ramah already fixed it at the Noah verse; the Masorah: only three lean wake-tokens in Scripture — Samson, Solomon, and the sleeper')
claim_en: THE FULL WAKING: וייקץ ('and Jacob AWOKE from his sleep,' 28:16) written with TWO yods per all the precise books and the Ramah's Noah-verse precedent; the Masorah's three lean wake-tokens (Samson's, Solomon's, the sleeper-psalm's) are all outside the Torah, named — the Torah wakes its sleepers full.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:16 ('וייקץ יעקב משנתו ויאמר — the final letters spell צבור: a person's prayer is heard only in congregation')
claim_en: THE CONGREGATION IN THE FINALS: the four words 'and Jacob AWOKE from his sleep and SAID' (28:16) end in the letters of צבור ('congregation') in order — the Kitzur's prayer-in-community teaching read off the verse's own last letters, at the place he will call the house of God.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:17 ('זה — with revia, not zaqef qatan')
claim_en: THE POINTING OF NONE-OTHER: זה in 'THIS is none other than the house of God' (28:17) carries revia (the resting dot-accent), not zaqef qatan (the small upright pause) — as Minchat Shai rules, letter-identical on SNAPSHOT.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:18 ('ויצק — Or Torah writes the tzadi SOFT, and so I saw in one manuscript; in other books with dagesh as the custom; see the Vayishlach verse')
claim_en: THE SECOND SPLIT-ATTESTED STATION: ויצק ('and he POURED oil on its top,' 28:18) — Minchat Shai records the books divided on the tzadi: Or Torah and one manuscript soft, the others with dagesh (the doubling dot). SNAPSHOT reads the tzadi SOFT — joining Or Torah's camp; the pour-verb's twin at the pillar's re-anointing (35:14) is the note's own cross-reference.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:20 ('לחם — with tevir, not with the lengthening stroke')
claim_en: THE VOW'S BREAD AS RULED: לחם ('bread to eat,' 28:20) carries tevir (the broken descending accent), not the meteg reading — Minchat Shai's ruling letter-identical on SNAPSHOT.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:20 ('וידר — three in the Masorah: Jacob vowed, Israel vowed, Jephthah vowed — the righteous vowed, and the FIRST to vow was Jacob; therefore the psalm says he swore to the MIGHTY ONE OF JACOB, for he opened the vows')
claim_en: THE FIRST VOWER: וידר ('and he VOWED') stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — Jacob at Bethel (28:20, the institution's birth) and Israel at Hormah (Num 21:2); the Masorah's third, Jephthah's, is Prophets-side, named. The Kitzur: the vow-psalm calls God 'the Mighty One of JACOB' because Jacob opened the vows — the census puts him first on the letter.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:20 ('ללבוש — two in the Masorah: here, and TO WEAR THE GARMENTS — teaching that Jacob was a high priest, as in Bereshit Rabbah: the Holy One said to Michael, you made My high priest blemished — you shall serve above in his place; and the service was in the firstborn, which he bought from Esau')
claim_en: THE HIGH PRIEST IN THE VOW'S GARMENT: ללבש ('a garment TO WEAR,' 28:20) — exactly TWO Torah tokens, and the second is the HIGH-PRIEST law's investiture clause (Lev 21:10, 'on whose head the anointing oil was poured... to WEAR the garments'): the Kitzur's Jacob-as-high-priest teaching rides a two-token census whose other end is the priesthood statute itself — beside the oil this unit pours on a head-stone.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:10 ('מבאר שבע — the Great Scriptures print the shin with patach and lists it among the book's rare pausal patach forms; in ALL the books qamatz, and so its rule at the pause; so Or Torah; the wedding-blood book wrote segol and multiplied words — THE WIND SHALL CARRY THEM ALL')
claim_en: SEVEN AT THE PAUSE: שבע of Beer-sheva (28:10) — the shin in qamatz (the long a) as all the books and Or Torah rule for the pausal position (the verse's rest sits on it); the printed patach and the segol book both rejected, in Minchat Shai's own words, 'the wind shall carry them all.'

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 28:10 (the long note: Sefer Tagi — 'Vayetze is continuous, neither open nor closed'; the Maimonidean gloss — the truth is a CLOSED break stands at the head of Vayetze and none within it, and so in all the famed Spanish codices) + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 28:10 ('some say this reading is closed because he went out in secret and fled in hiding')
claim_en: THE CLOSED FLIGHT (manual): whether a closed paragraph-break precedes 'and Jacob went out' (28:10) is the era's manuscript question — Sefer Tagi against the Spanish codices — and the Kitzur reads the closedness as the flight's own secrecy; the paragraph layer is uninstrumented on SNAPSHOT (standing gap).

source: Bereshit Rabbah 68:8
claim_en: THE TRADITION STATES THE GRAMMAR RULE OUR MORPHOLOGY LAYER RUNS, AND STATES IT AS A RULE. R. Nechemya: any word that would need the preposition 'to' at its start may instead take a heh at its end - and he gives four examples, to Sodom, to Seir, to Egypt, to Haran, the last being this verse's own final word. Machine-checked against our corpus: the morphology layer tags that ending as a directional suffix and finds 392 such tokens in the Torah across 75 distinct forms, and ALL FOUR of the chain's cited examples are among them. The chain's recorded objection - that one word carries both the preposition and the ending - is answered rather than suppressed. This is the sharpest overlap yet between the tradition's own inference rules and this project's machine layer: not a claim the machine can check, but the same rule, arrived at independently and stated in words.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 69:4
claim_en: A NUMERIC CLAIM OPENED UNDER GUARD 3: THE COUNT DID NOT REPRODUCE UNDER THE FRAME TRIED, BUT ITS EDGE CASE DID, EXACTLY. The chain holds the patriarchs are named eighteen times in the Torah and that the eighteen blessings of the prayer were fixed against them, and it records both audit branches - one who counts nineteen must EXCLUDE our 28:13, because Jacob is not named in it; one who counts seventeen must admit a later verse. Under the frame this derivation tried - Torah verses naming all three patriarchs together - our corpus returns nine, or ten if the alternate name is allowed, not eighteen. THE COUNT IS THEREFORE NOT GRADED HERE: the frame is stated and the leg left open, because twice in this project a count that looked wrong was a wrong frame rather than a wrong tradition. What IS machine-checked is the edge case the chain hangs its audit on: 28:13 names Abraham and Isaac and does NOT name Jacob, exactly as the exclusion branch requires.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 68:11
claim_en: THE STONES ARE COUNTED THREE WAYS, AND EACH COUNT IS A TEST THE SLEEPER SETS. Twelve, on R. Yehuda's reading, as a test for twelve tribes; three, on R. Nechemya's, as a test of the name-designation; two at minimum, on the Rabbis', as a no-waste test - Abraham produced one unfit son, Isaac produced one, will I produce waste? The fusion into one stone answers whichever test was set. The chain then disputes how long he had not lain down, fourteen years or twenty, and what he recited through them, the fifteen songs of ascent or the whole Psalter. Four numeric disputes on one night, none resolved.

check.note: Three incompatible counts of the same objects, each framed as a different test, with the miracle answering all three.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 68:12
claim_en: A DREAM-LAW RULING IS SEATED ON THE DREAM VERSE. The teaching that DREAMS FOLLOW THE INTERPRETATION - that the content of a dream has no effect until it is interpreted - is placed at 28:12, with the case of the beam-counting interpreter. A standing ruling about the legal status of dreams anchored to the corpus's most famous dream.

check.note: A ruling on the legal status of dream-content anchored to the archetypal dream verse.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 68:10
claim_en: TWO HOURS ARE TAKEN FROM THE DAY AND BOOKED FOR REPAYMENT LATER IN THE CORPUS. The sun is said to have set two hours early so that the meeting could be private, and the chain does not leave the debt open: the two hours are repaid at 32:32, where the sun rose for him. The claim is then generalized - you are a sign for your children - with an exile sunset and a return sunrise cited from the prophets. A borrowed quantity, tracked to its restoration in a block not yet derived.

check.note: A quantity of time removed at one verse and explicitly restored at another, with the pair read as a sign.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 69:6
claim_en: THE CHAIN RUNS THE SAME CLAUSE-MAP THIS MACHINE RUNS, AND FINDS ONE CLAUSE UNCOVERED. It sets the promise of 28:15 against the vow of 28:20-22 clause by clause - with-me against with-me, keep against keep, return against return - and reports that every clause of the vow is answered by the promise EXCEPT SUSTENANCE. The dissent is recorded: R. Isi holds that 'I will not forsake you' IS the sustenance clause. This is the tradition performing a promise-input against vow-output diff and reporting a single unmatched field, which is exactly the shape of this project's own demand ledger.

check.note: A clause-by-clause diff of a promise against a vow, reporting one uncovered clause, with a dissent that closes it.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 70:1; Bereshit Rabbah 70:3
claim_en: THE VOW IS TREATED AS AN INSTITUTION WITH A CHAIN OF TITLE AND A LEDGER. This is read as the first vow, and 'saying' is read as saying TO THE GENERATIONS - vowing in a time of distress - so that all vows are ascribed to this vower and not to his fathers, proved from a psalm that names him and not them. A four-vow ledger is then kept: two vowed and lost, two vowed and profited, with this vow filed on the LOSS side. The tradition maintains a register of a legal instrument's instances and grades them.

check.note: A legal instrument given a first instance, a chain of title, and a graded register of later instances.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 81:1
claim_en: THE ENFORCEMENT SIDE OF THE VOW IS RECORDED, AND IT EXPLAINS THE LOSS. R. Yanai's rule is that delay in discharging a vow triggers an audit of the vower's ledger - scrutiny follows vows - and consecrated property carries a curse on whoever benefits from it. This is why the vow of this block is filed as a loss rather than a profit: the penalty is not for vowing but for the interval before payment, which the corpus later marks with a command to arise and go up.

check.note: A delay penalty that explains an earlier grading, connecting the vow to a later command in the corpus.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 70:7
claim_en: A TITHE ARITHMETIC IS CHALLENGED FROM OUTSIDE AND ANSWERED WITH A COUNT. The objection is put by a Samaritan: the tithe promise cannot be honoured, because Levi is one tribe of twelve and that is not a tenth. The answer is a recount - the tribes are FOURTEEN once the two Joseph tribes are separated, and then the four firstborn of the four mothers are removed because the firstborn is already sacred and SACRED DOES NOT TITHE SACRED - leaving ten, of which Levi is the tenth. A promise audited by arithmetic and defended by a rule of exclusion.

check.note: A tithe promise challenged numerically and rescued by a recount plus a sanctity-exclusion rule.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 68:14
claim_en: THE LADDER IS READ AS A SEQUENCE OF EMPIRES, WITH THE WORD ORDER CARRYING THE ARGUMENT. The dream is mapped onto a later vision's four-metal image, and the reason ascending is written before descending is given as structural: each kingdom stands LOWER than the one before it, so the ascent of each is also a descent. The eternal kingdom is then read into the standing figure at the ladder's head. A second schema for the same exile machine the corpus builds at gen_47's tribe-against-kingdom table.

check.note: A dream image mapped onto a kingdom sequence, with the verse's word order supplying the descending argument.

source: Onkelos Genesis 28:13; Onkelos Genesis 28:16
claim_en: THE TRANSLATION INSERTS A BUFFER AT BOTH THEOPHANY VERSES. Where the verse has the LORD standing over him, Onkelos has the GLORY of the LORD standing; where he says the LORD is in this place, Onkelos has the GLORY of the LORD DWELLING there. The anti-anthropomorphic policy fires twice in three verses, and the same rendering separately softens his admission of not having known.

check.note: An anti-anthropomorphic buffer applied consistently at both theophany verses of one scene.

source: Onkelos Genesis 28:15; Onkelos Genesis 28:20
claim_en: THE TRANSLATION TAKES A SIDE IN THE ORDER DISPUTE BY MAKING THE VOW QUOTE THE PROMISE. The chain disputes whether the vow's 'if' expresses doubt, given that the promise had already been made. Onkelos renders the promise as MY WORD IS YOUR SUPPORT and then renders the vow's condition in the same words - if the WORD of the LORD will be my support - so that the condition verbatim quotes the promise it is said to doubt. The rendering thereby settles the dispute in favour of the reading that the 'if' conditions the discharge, not the trust.

check.note: A translation resolving an exegetical dispute by making a condition quote the promise word for word.

source: Onkelos Genesis 28:17; Onkelos Genesis 28:22
claim_en: THE HOUSE OF GOD IS DE-LITERALIZED INTO A DOCTRINE OF PRAYER-RECEPTION. Onkelos renders it NOT A COMMON PLACE but a place of FAVOUR before the LORD, with the gate OPPOSITE heaven; the stone that will be a house of God becomes the stone ON WHICH I WILL WORSHIP BEFORE the LORD; and the tithe given 'to You' becomes given BEFORE You. Every locative claim about the divine is converted into a claim about where prayer is received - converging with the reading that the ladder's incline reached the Temple.

check.note: Locative divine language systematically converted into prayer-reception language across one scene.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 69:8
claim_en: A CITY IS GIVEN STANDING PROPERTIES THAT HOLD ACROSS THE WHOLE CORPUS. The place is identified with a city that no conqueror could scatter or destroy and over which the angel of death has no dominion, so that its elders are carried outside the wall to die; with four accounts of its name, and a hidden entrance beneath an almond tree over a cave. A place entity carrying permanent attributes rather than a single scene's description.

check.note: A place given permanent, corpus-wide properties including immunity claims and an access rule.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 68:6
claim_en: A DEPARTURE RULE IS STATED AND THEN DEFENDED AGAINST ITS OWN COUNTEREXAMPLE. When a righteous person leaves a city, the city's radiance and glory leave with them - and the objection is obvious, since this city still held two righteous inhabitants. The answer is a comparison maxim: the merit of one righteous person is not like the merit of two. The rule survives by being made relative rather than absolute.

check.note: A departure rule rescued from its counterexample by converting an absolute claim into a comparative one.
